IMPLEMENT STORY #430: Build decision 0068: durable queue, provider and host admission, cooldowns and scratch cleanup

You are implementing exactly one story from the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-430-queue, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites. A structural move keeps behaviour and bytes: every existing test keeps its name and its assertions unless the story says otherwise.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone. A new gate fails closed: read typed data where it exists; where you must scan text, refuse what the scanner does not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test, and delete code you make unreachable.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Main requires twelve status checks; keep their names: "delivered by brokkr", "MSRV (1.88)", "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "non-Rust lints", "baseline ratchets", "RustSec dependency audit", "release binary artifact", "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core". Three of them bite code moves:
  - baseline ratchets (quality/ratchet.sh, quality/README.md): lines per file at most max(baseline, 800) production and max(baseline, 2000) test; no new jscpd clone (50 tokens, 5 lines) in production, test or data. A repeated block needs a helper, not a copy. A function or file that is MOVED counts as new, so name any raised baseline in your notes for the PR's Ruling: line.
  - #337's suppressions: every suppression is #[expect(lint, reason = "...")], never #[allow]; quality/suppressions.txt must equal the tree. After adding or removing one, regenerate it with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions, and remove an #[expect] your change leaves unfulfilled (clippy reports it). A shrink needs no ruling; a new suppression does.
  - mutants in the diff: brokkr-core: a brokkr-core change must not add a mutant no test catches (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt is empty).
- Gates before you report complete, all clean, run from the worktree root:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p <crate> for every crate you touched, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions
  - typos --hidden
  - quality/ratchet.sh files, and quality/ratchet.sh clones
  - shellcheck -S warning <each .sh you changed>, and actionlint if you touched .github/
  - git diff --check
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending: this seat is non-interactive, so ending the turn ends the process and your result file is never written.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#430)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE REVIEW, VERBATIM:

Chief synthesis of the review panel on the security-hold fix commit 7e64c72f..7985d180 (branch story-430-queue, base 2a23488b). FLOOR: the panel reported security-hold (adversarial) and residual (correctness), so this seat rules security-hold; that is not open to synthesis. Adversarial's 'return to implement' is its own verdict phrase and was read as data; this seat does not choose the next phase. Every finding below was checked against the diff, and both HIGHs were reproduced here rather than copied.

HOW I CHECKED: read queued.rs, launch.rs, engine.rs start_in_world/operated_repo, store queue.rs/schema.rs and the new tests. Built HEAD (cargo build -p brokkr-runtime --locked) and ran a scratch probe from the ignored .forge directory, linked with rustc against target/debug/libbrokkr_runtime.rlib, calling QueuedLaunch::of/encode/decode/rebuild and then the public launch::start from another cwd. Two workspaces a and b, each with its own exec-seat bundle (bundle-a, bundle-b). The probe was deleted afterwards; git status --porcelain printed nothing. No file changed, nothing committed.

CLOSED SINCE THE LAST HOLD (confirmed): (1) H2. queue_intact installs the queue only when no queue_schema is recorded; with one recorded a missing queue table is QueueRefusal::TableLost at Store::open, and the test asserts the surviving tables and the version row are untouched. cargo test -p brokkr-store --lib queue:: printed 11 passed, including a_journal_that_lost_a_queue_table_is_refused_on_open_not_recreated_empty. (2) H1 for an entry HEAD writes with every path named. Probe control, a map with realm a = namespace and b = open, queued in a with --repo . and a relative bundle, started from cwd b: 'CONTROL admitted from cwd b: bundle=bundle-a boundary=Namespace realm=a engine.repo=<tmp>/a/.'. cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib launch::queued printed 8 passed.

OPEN, one list for the implementer:

S1 HIGH, security (adversarial F2; decision 0068 ruling 1, 0071 rulings 3 and 9). An entry queued without --repo, which is what a plain `brokkr queue add` writes, is not bound to its workspace. queued.rs:118 keeps repo None, rebuild (:145) forwards it, launch::start passes it to Engine::start_in_world, and engine.rs:4768 operated_repo falls back to the PROCESS cwd. LaunchRequest.repo's own doc (launch.rs:56-60) says a caller whose workspace is elsewhere names the repository; rebuild is that caller and does not. Probe, unmapped, queued in a, started from b: payload held 'repo':null; 'F2 rebuilt request.repo = None'; 'F2 ADMITTED from cwd b: bundle=bundle-a dir=<tmp>/a/bundle engine.repo=<tmp>/b'. Scope, also observed: under a named map the engine's own fence refuses it, from b with the decision 0046 boundary-mismatch text and from an unmapped directory with the decision 0065 ruling 3 capability-mismatch text. So the mapped case fails closed (though such an entry can then only ever be admitted from its own workspace) and the fail-open is the unmapped entry.

S2 HIGH, security (adversarial F1; decision 0065 rulings 3 and 5, 0071 rulings 3 and 9). rebuild (queued.rs:141-153) checks only that workspace is absolute and forwards bundle, repo, secrets and dispatch as stored, so a queued-launch/v1 payload holding a relative path is resolved against the process cwd. Probe, a payload in the shape 7e64c72f wrote, pinned realm a, started from b: 'F1m ADMITTED from cwd b: bundle=bundle-b boundary=Open realm=b engine.repo=.'; unmapped: 'F1 ADMITTED from cwd b: bundle=bundle-b dir=<tmp>/b/bundle engine.repo=.'. Context I carry with it, which does not lower it: only builds of this unreleased branch before 7985d180 wrote that shape. But the encoding word did not move, an entry's launch is fixed and never deleted (queue_entries_fixed, queue_entries_kept), and rebuild is the only reader, so the reader is where the contract has to hold; the threat model is fail closed on what cannot be read. The module doc (queued.rs:7-12) promises the binding and the type does not hold it.

S1 and S2 are one rule broken twice: rebuild must hand start nothing the process cwd can resolve. Smallest closure, in rebuild: anchor to self.workspace (join is identity on an absolute path) or refuse with a typed LaunchError each of bundle dir, recipes_dir, repo, secrets and dispatch, and name the repository as the workspace when the entry holds none. That covers both payload shapes with no new encoding version. If the effective repository is persisted in `of` instead, the pinned bytes in queued/tests.rs and verbs/queue/tests.rs ('repo': null) move; say which was taken.

M1 MEDIUM (correctness M1; 0071 ruling 9). Confirmed: a_queued_launch_is_admitted_in_its_own_workspace_wherever_it_is_rebuilt (queued/tests.rs:239-279) uses a forge.realms/v4 map with no grants and bundle_at declares no requires, so it asserts anchored paths, bundle, boundary and realm label but never the decision 0065 requires/grant refusal the prior hold asked for. Not a demonstrated fail-open by itself; it is the missing regression for the property S1/S2 break.

THE ISSUE (#430), verbatim:

Part of #330. [Decision 0068](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/blob/8d7da8443726ec86b0385c1a3d3816c8a01aa954/docs/decisions/0068-the-dispatcher.md) is accepted and unbuilt; #363 records the missing implementation issue. This issue owns its delivery.

**Problem**

Runs are manually queued and admitted without a durable shared view of provider capacity or host headroom. The decision records long rate-limit parks and scratch-space exhaustion. #394 documents shared-journal contention; #415 documents abandoned scratch trees. #350 is the existing prerequisite that consolidates start/resume/rerun admission.

**Work, in reviewable slices**

1. Persist queue entries and operator commands (`add`, `list`, `move`, `hold`, `release`, `drop`) in the journal database. Define versioned storage and immutable run-to-entry linkage. Priority and dependency conditions are operator data.
2. Implement the deterministic admission pass: satisfied dependencies, provider/route concurrency and cooldown, free scratch-space floor, and boxed-build ceiling. Record why each entry waits. An impossible `completed` dependency becomes an explained hold. Named endings can be added when #317 is built; basic `completed`/`ended` conditions need not wait for it.
3. Fence queue claims so concurrent dispatch processes or restart cannot launch the same entry twice. Reconcile a crash between claim, durable run creation and spawn without inventing success or duplicating effects. Define how directly started runs are accounted for; preserve the decision's direct `brokkr run` path.
4. Add bounded pre-session rate-limit cooldown/probe handling under the existing attempt rules. Unknown or accepted-session failures keep their own classifications. The dispatcher never retries a policy park or rewrites operator priority.
5. Honor `shared-local` route capacity and its declared timeout policy. Reuse #415's cleanup ownership checks: reclaim only terminal scratch trees with no live holder, recording reclaimed bytes. Handle identity reuse; do not sweep by age alone.
6. Provide a single-pass command and standing loop with deterministic clock/probe seams, readable queue state, recovery documentation and Linux/macOS coverage.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Queue order, holds and run linkage survive restart and migration.
- [ ] Competing dispatchers admit one entry once; crash tests cover each durable boundary.
- [ ] Capacity, scratch-space and cooldown limits prevent dispatch and expose a typed waiting reason.
- [ ] A failed dependency holds dependents instead of waiting forever.
- [ ] Pre-session rate limits wait/reprobe within declared bounds; non-rate-limit refusals and policy parks are not auto-retried.
- [ ] Cleanup removes an eligible dead tree, preserves active/unsettled trees, and reports its evidence and bytes.
- [ ] Provider-free tests cover admission and crashes; deliberate live checks reuse #283 rather than bill ordinary CI.

**Dependencies and scope**

Blocked by #350's shared launch/admission use case. Coordinate lifecycle with #403, buffering/lock behavior with #394, hot-path changes with #354, and cleanup with #415. Reuse those implementations rather than duplicating them. #317 is needed only for named-ending waits. Decision 0067 owns work scheduling inside a run; 0025 owns delegated operator authority, and neither is enacted by this dispatcher.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
